title: Track inspector re-seeds untouched clip start and downbeat when the stored value changes
acceptance: When the stored clipStartMs or beatAnchorMs of the selected track changes underneath the open track inspector (e.g. a clip-window or downbeat edit made outside the inspector), an untouched Clip start / Downbeat field shows the new value.
A later unrelated inspector Save (e.g. notes) does not re-send the stale clipStartMs or beatAnchorMs, mirroring RF-90's startOffsetMs fix; a deliberately edited value is still sent.
nextAction: Confirm whether any surface besides the inspector can change clipStartMs or beatAnchorMs while the inspector is open; if one can, apply RF-90's value-based re-seed-and-omit rule (Dashboard.tsx TrackInspector, startAtFieldValue / startAtStoredMs, with the value-based rule from #650) to those two fields with a fail-first test. If none can, cancel with that finding.

evidence.summary: Logged from RF-90: the inspector seeds clipStart and downbeat once per track id, the same stale-seed shape that caused B-1 for startOffsetMs. Not reproduced; RF-90 fixed only startOffsetMs, the field a timeline drag moves.
